slides.title: Public-Private Cooperation in the Port of Rotterdam: An Agent-Based Toy Model of Cooperative Efforts Against Cocaine Trafficking
slides.highlight: This study uses an agent-based model to analyze public-private cooperation dynamics, demonstrating that coordinated multi-parameter strategies significantly outperform isolated measures in complex societal systems.

card.one_liner: Agent-based modeling shows coordinated multi-parameter strategies outperform isolated measures in port security cooperation.
card.key_idea: Coupled ABM and CLD model trust, cooperation, and enforcement dynamics to simulate public-private cooperation effectiveness.
card.evaluation: Simulated parameter shocks over five years; coordinated strategies yielded 25% effectiveness gain versus 13% for isolated cooperation.
card.limitation: Exploratory toy model lacking empirical validation; results depend on specific initial configurations and structural assumptions.

slides.title: BEARING: Who Is Talking to Whom? Grounding Acoustic Direction in Vision for Online Multi-Party Conversation
slides.tldr: ONLINE ACOUSTIC-VISUAL DIRECTION FUSION FOR MULTI-PARTY CONVERSATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces BEARING, a geometry-first system that grounds acoustic direction in vision to enable online speaker and addressee identification in multi-party conversations, directly addressing HyECHO's need for robust, non-data-hungry social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: BEARING grounds acoustic direction in vision to improve online multi-party speaker and addressee detection.
card.key_idea: Registers microphone array direction into camera images as visual prompts and verifiable rewards for vision-language model alignment.
card.evaluation: Tested on AMI, EasyCom, and AVDIAR; direction prompts boost speaker accuracy 54% to 74%, outperforming self-evaluation rewards.
card.limitation: Addressee detection remains difficult due to linguistic dependencies; online registration learning causes initial accuracy dips.

slides.title: EvoMisty: Building, Optimizing, and Evolving Capabilities on a Social Robot
slides.highlight: EvoMisty enables social robots to autonomously build, optimize, and reuse capabilities via LLM-driven coding agents, directly supporting RwB's goal of AI-mediated embodied learning and adaptive human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: EvoMisty enables coding agents to autonomously build, optimize, and evolve robot capabilities from documentation.
card.key_idea: A plugin framework where agents construct verified atomic capabilities, optimize tasks via metric-driven loops, and distill reusable skills.
card.evaluation: Tested on Misty II with Claude Code and Codex; completed 35 tasks, improved 7 metrics, and demonstrated cross-task skill reuse.
card.limitation: Validated only on Misty II; relies on human feedback for verification and final performance depends on initial agent implementation.

slides.title: Unifying Partner and Environment Diversity to Improve Human-AI Coordination
slides.highlight: This paper introduces Cross Environment Co-Play (CECP), a framework that jointly models partner and environment diversity to enhance zero-shot coordination, achieving state-of-the-art results on the Overcooked benchmark relevant to ADAM-CHAT's evaluation protocols.

card.one_liner: CECP unifies partner and environment diversity to improve zero-shot human-AI coordination.
card.key_idea: Two-stage training: self-play partners across diverse environments, then cooperator trained against them with next-state prediction.
card.evaluation: Tested on Foraging and Overcooked with held-out partners/environments; outperformed baselines in AI-AI and human-AI coordination.
card.limitation: Performance depends on diversity of training partners/environments; latents capture broad skill rather than fine-grained intent.

slides.title: Realbotix launches humanoid robots for education, wellness and companionship
slides.highlight: Realbotix has introduced humanoid robots designed for education, wellness, and companionship, highlighting the growing market for social robotics.

slides.title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Neon AI Model
slides.highlight: Google has released the Gemini 4 Neon AI model, which is positioned as a rival to Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol.

slides.title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation
slides.highlight: This paper identifies a 'bias cascade' where LLM agents aligned with social knowledge still fail to replicate collective effects in simulations, a critical challenge for MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: LLMs accurately predict social intervention effects but fail to replicate them in multi-agent simulations due to bias cascades.
card.key_idea: Introduces REFLEX benchmark to compare knowledge judgment against effect simulation, revealing that state and action mismatches cascade into divergent macro outcomes.
card.evaluation: Assessed 8 LLMs on 30 counterfactual tasks; best model scored 0.847 in judgment vs 0.453 in simulation, with significant gaps confirmed via bootstrap.
card.limitation: Current methods cannot reliably simulate collective behavior; providing explicit knowledge or increasing population size does not significantly improve effect replication.

slides.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
slides.highlight: This work introduces an audiovisual LLM that unifies speaker identification and utterance timing, directly addressing the need for precise diarization and addressee modeling in hybrid team interactions.

card.one_liner: DiaCap jointly learns utterance timing and audiovisual diarization via SFT and RL, achieving high timestamp accuracy.
card.key_idea: Unifies timing and speaker attribution in one model, trained on synthetic dense captions and refined by RL with fine-grained rewards.
card.evaluation: Tested on extended DiaDemBench; outperforms Gemini 4 Argon in timestamps (76.59 vs 42.76) and matches diarization accuracy.
card.limitation: Struggles with small/distant faces and relies on off-the-shelf transcripts, where errors degrade diarization performance.

slides.title: StreamCoach: Proactive Sports Coaching via Continuous Visual Reasoning
slides.highlight: StreamCoach demonstrates a streaming action quality assessment framework that uses continuous chain-of-thought reasoning to provide timely, holistic coaching feedback, relevant to MOSAIC's goal of adaptive AI coaching for human skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: StreamCoach uses continuous chain-of-thought reasoning to provide timely, evidence-gated sports coaching feedback.
card.key_idea: A streaming framework coupling Technique-Aware Reasoning with Holistic Coaching, optimized via Temporal-Semantic Alignment Reinforcement Learning.
card.evaluation: Benchmarked on EE4D-Stream (1,213 Ego-Exo4D clips) against 11 baselines; achieves SOTA in timing, assessment, and coaching quality.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-assisted dataset construction and proprietary models for evaluation, potentially introducing annotation or judgment biases.

slides.title: YYForce Launches Six Seven Humanoid Concierge for Novotel Singapore
slides.highlight: The deployment of a humanoid concierge in a hospitality setting provides a real-world case study for human-robot interaction and embodied social robotics.

slides.title: Google DeepMind Releases Genie 4
slides.highlight: Google DeepMind has released Genie 4, a world model that allows users to modify the environment from within the scene.

slides.title: EMIP: Embodied Multi-Party Interaction Platform
slides.highlight: This paper introduces EMIP, a Minecraft-based virtual environment that supports full-duplex speech and simultaneous physical interaction among multiple humans and AI agents. It provides a reusable platform for studying human-agent and agent-agent cooperation, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: EMIP is a Minecraft-based platform enabling concurrent speech and physical interaction among multiple humans and AI agents.
card.key_idea: Client-server architecture with MCP interfaces for observation, action, and audio, supporting full-duplex speech and simultaneous physical tasks.
card.evaluation: Demonstrated via usage examples of concurrent speech and coordination; no quantitative benchmarks or baseline comparisons reported.
card.limitation: Performance constrained by LLM inference and audio processing times, limiting simulation speedup in long-term experiments.

slides.title: Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas Reading Posts on X
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that LLM personas systematically penalize identical text based on the attributed speaker's identity, mirroring human ideological congruence. This is relevant to HyECHO as it highlights how synthetic agents process source cues and identity signals, informing the design of non-data-hungry models for social perception and addressee modeling in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: LLM personas penalize political posts based on speaker identity, mirroring human ideological congruence.
card.key_idea: Fully crossed experiment varying speaker attribution (Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal) on identical anonymized X posts judged by value-grounded LLM personas.
card.evaluation: 322k persona-post quartets using gpt-oss-20b; validated against 48 CIS barometers via ordinal leader rankings and ideological congruence contrasts.
card.limitation: Personas reflect dated political priors (pre-2024 cutoff), failing to capture recent shifts in right-wing voter preferences.

slides.title: NVIDIA Releases Alpamayo 2 Edge
slides.highlight: NVIDIA has released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2B parameter reasoning Vision-Language-Action model designed for DRIVE Thor.

slides.title: LookAnything: A Foundation Model for Holistic Gaze Following
slides.tldr: Foundation model for holistic gaze following
slides.highlight: This work introduces a foundation model for holistic gaze following that supports diverse outputs and reasoning, directly addressing the need for robust attention and intent understanding in human-robot interaction scenarios relevant to embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: LookAnything unifies gaze tasks via learnable priors, outperforming VLMs and matching specialists.
card.key_idea: Foundation model using learnable gaze-prior queries to internalize depth and geometry, eliminating auxiliary inputs for holistic gaze following.
card.evaluation: Tested on HoliGaze-Bench (33 VLMs) and 5 native benchmarks; outperforms VLMs, matches specialists, and validates OOD generalization.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic data engine for training; real-world robustness shown only via limited robot deployment.

slides.title: Putting a Robot on a Phone Call: Layered Signaling, Bounded Occupancy and Turn Arbitration over WebRTC
slides.highlight: This paper details a WebRTC-based architecture for robot voice calls, featuring layered signaling and turn arbitration mechanisms that could inform the communication infrastructure for hybrid human-AI team interactions.

card.one_liner: A WebRTC-based robot voice call system using layered signaling, bounded occupancy, and turn arbitration.
card.key_idea: Separates signaling, media, and speech routes; uses credential prefetch, concurrent setup, session slots, speaker locks, and a 2s gate for turn arbitration.
card.evaluation: Tested on one iPhone/Safari with Wi-Fi/cellular; measured readiness times, occupancy recovery, and simulated controller timing; no user study or acoustic validation.
card.limitation: Single-device/browser scope, simulated controller decisions, unmeasured acoustic output, and identified feedback association errors in asynchronous boundaries.

slides.title: VidForce: Predicting Force-Aware Articulation by Observing Humans
slides.highlight: VidForce estimates interaction trajectories and force profiles from third-person RGB video, aligning with MOSAIC's goal of deriving physics-based skill metrics from visual observations.

card.one_liner: VidForce predicts articulated object trajectories and force profiles from third-person human video using learned physical prototypes.
card.key_idea: Uses learned force prototypes and a joint conditional flow to refine trajectories and force estimates from video, transferring supervision from paired instrumented gripper data.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Hoi! dataset against baselines; achieves 6.6 cm ATE and 4.81 N peak-force MAE, with successful real-world robot deployment.
card.limitation: Relies on paired human-gripper recordings for supervision; accuracy degrades on heavy interactions and assumes shared object-action sets force requirements.

slides.title: Do Vision-Language Models Know Their Own Visual Weaknesses? Probing Capability-Level Metacognition
slides.highlight: The study reveals that Vision-Language Models largely fail to predict their own visual weaknesses before attempting tasks, though implicit signals in answer probabilities emerge during solving. This distinction between stated predictions and latent self-knowledge is critical for ADAM-CHAT's goal of developing AI teammates with robust meta-cognition and self-correction capabilities.

card.one_liner: VLMs lack self-awareness of visual weaknesses, but answer probabilities reveal model-specific limitations.
card.key_idea: Probes VLM metacognition by separating shared task difficulty from model-specific weaknesses using accuracy predictions and answer probabilities.
card.evaluation: Tested 33 VLMs on 13 visual axes; found predictions poor, but answer probabilities correlate with model-specific weaknesses.
card.limitation: Stated predictions fail to capture model-specific weaknesses; only internal answer probabilities reveal them, requiring access to logits.

slides.title: Read My Lips: Context-aware Lip Reading Using Language and Audio-Visual Models
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how combining lip-reading, language modeling, and audio-visual generation can recover speech in noisy or partially observable conditions, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: RML combines lip reading, language models, and audio-visual generation to restore speech from corrupted or missing audio.
card.key_idea: Integrates visual articulation hypotheses, linguistic context, and acoustic evidence via adaptive selection to reconstruct synchronized speech.
card.evaluation: Tested on TalkVid and VoxMM across noise, silence, and hard-to-read lips; outperforms lip readers and speech editors on WER and span recovery.
card.limitation: Performance relies on lip reader accuracy; struggles when visual evidence is unreliable and audio is heavily corrupted, requiring context inference.

slides.title: ClusterVAD: Threshold-Free Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection with Pre-Trained Neural Representations
slides.tldr: UNSUPERVISED VAD VIA FROZEN FOUNDATION MODELS
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that frozen speech foundation model representations can enable robust, unsupervised voice activity detection without labeled data or manual thresholds, addressing domain shift issues in noisy or far-field environments. Such threshold-free VAD is a foundational component for reliable diarization and social perception in hybrid human-AI team settings.

card.one_liner: ClusterVAD achieves robust unsupervised voice activity detection by clustering frozen speech foundation model representations.
card.key_idea: Clusters SSL features via k-means, labels them using sonority, and applies a threshold-free HMM decision for frame-level speech probability.
card.evaluation: Tested on 12 diverse benchmarks (AMI, AliMeeting, Torgo, etc.) against supervised/unsupervised baselines using DetER and Event-F1 metrics.
card.limitation: High computational cost due to SSL encoders; threshold-free decision is less reliable on short utterances; limited language diversity in codebook.

slides.title: Contact Geometry for Generative Models: An Unbalanced Optimal Transport Formulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces Contact unbalanced Optimal Transport (CuOT), which uses contact geometry to eliminate structural bias in unpaired data generation, offering a stable alternative to Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao methods. It is relevant to MOSAIC as it provides a robust mathematical framework for aligning intent and estimating proficiency via Optimal Transport in scenarios with imperfect data pairing.

card.one_liner: Contact geometry-based unbalanced optimal transport eliminates structural bias and mode collapse in generative models.
card.key_idea: Decouples transport direction from mass growth using contact geometry, adapting step sizes to local density to prevent overshooting.
card.evaluation: Validated on biological dynamics, image translation, and video generation; outperforms WFR-based UOT and OT baselines in stability and accuracy.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Ego2Real: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Visuo-Tactile Demonstrations
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that integrating tactile sensing with egocentric views significantly improves the fidelity of hand-object interaction reconstruction and policy learning, directly supporting MOSAIC's goal of estimating procedural skill through multi-view and physics-based data.

card.one_liner: Ego2Real transfers bimanual dexterous skills from egocentric visuo-tactile demos via tactile-guided reconstruction and contact-informed RL.
card.key_idea: Refines hand-object reconstruction using tactile gloves to resolve visual ambiguities, then trains residual RL policies with region-wise contact rewards.
card.evaluation: Validated on two bimanual tasks in simulation and real-world, outperforming REGRIND and baselines in success rates and contact fidelity.
card.limitation: Requires specific tactile gloves, known object meshes, and simulation; currently limited to rigid objects and single-demo policies.

slides.title: Preserving Prosody in Speaker Anonymization
slides.highlight: This work improves the tradeoff between speaker obfuscation and prosodic content preservation, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Integrating a speaker-disentangled prosody encoder into CosyVoice2 enables prosody-preserving speaker anonymization.
card.key_idea: Conditioning CosyVoice2's LLM and flow-matching modules on low-rate, speaker-normalized prosody embeddings extracted via a self-supervised encoder.
card.evaluation: Human perceptual tests (94.3% intent accuracy) and VoicePrivacy 2026 metrics (ASV EER, WER, pitch correlation) on LibriSpeech.
card.limitation: Trade-off exists: prosody control in the LLM reduces anonymization efficacy compared to flow-matching-only or baseline systems.

slides.title: Can Speech LLMs Recognize When Audio Evidence Is Insufficient? A Diagnostic Study and a Pre-Generation Probing Mitigation
slides.tldr: Speech LLMs hallucinate on unanswerable audio; probing mitigates this.
slides.highlight: This study reveals that speech LLMs frequently hallucinate answers when audio evidence is insufficient, a failure mode that persists even with human recordings. It proposes pre-generation attention probing as a mitigation strategy, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception by ensuring models can accurately assess the sufficiency of audio inputs for state estimation.

card.one_liner: Speech LLMs hallucinate on unanswerable audio; pre-generation probing detects this better than sampling.
card.key_idea: Quantifies synthetic audio bias in diagnostics and uses ridge probes on frozen prompt states to predict hallucinations before generation.
card.evaluation: Tested Qwen2-Audio and ASR cascades on SQuAD 2.0; probe achieved 0.773 AUROC, outperforming semantic entropy (chance).
card.limitation: Small dataset (25 probe items), selection bias in probe configuration, and results specific to Qwen models and one TTS system.

slides.title: Self-Sensing Compliant Anthropomorphic Hand for Speed-Dictated Shared Force Control in Teleoperation
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that mechanical compliance in tendon-driven hands can serve as an intrinsic sensing resource for force estimation, enabling shared-control teleoperation without external tactile sensors.

card.one_liner: Compliant hand uses tendon springs for self-sensing, enabling speed-based shared force control in VR teleoperation.
card.key_idea: Series springs in tendon routing act as sensors to estimate joint states and forces, allowing grasp force regulation based on operator closing speed.
card.evaluation: Validated via force estimation accuracy, speed classification, and teleoperation tasks with fragile/heavy objects, showing improved grasp success rates.
card.limitation: Force estimation accuracy decreases for proximal phalanx contacts, and speed classification relies on empirical thresholds that may vary with object stiffness.
